Vs.

full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner is against judgment and decree dated 24.2.88 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Bhola in Title Appeal No. 11 of 1986 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 21.12.85 passed by the Munsif, Borhanuddin Upazila in Title Suit No. 163 of 1984. 

 2. Short question involved in this Rule is whether Court of appeal below was justified in holding that plaintiff-petitioner has no locus standi for declaring decree passed in an earlier Title Suit No. 26 of 1977 in which he was not a party and no relief was granted against him as not binding on him and in setting aside the decree of the trial Court on such erroneous view. 

 3. In this case admittedly defendant-opposite party No. 1 was appointed temporary Nikah Registerar on 1.11.75 under Rule 5(1) of the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Rules, 1974 and his appointment was cancelled by Memo dated 10.1.77. Admittedly, the said memo cancelling his temporary licence was declared illegal and the defendant-opposite party Nos. 2-5 were restrained from interfering with the work of the opposite party No. 1 as Nikah Registrar and giving effect to the said order of cancellation. It is true that in the said suit filed on 21.1.77 plaintiff-petitioner was not added as a defendant but he was appointed permanent Nikah Registrar on 10.9.81 under Rule 5 (4) of the said Rules. Petitioner filed Title Suit No. 107 of 1983 subsequently re-numbered as Title Suit No. 163 of 1984 challenging the said decree as he was directed by the Deputy Commissioner, Bhola to take steps for setting aside the said decree. Though the Court of appeal below observed that the petitioner was appointed perm anent Nikah Registrar after the temporary injunction passed in Title Suit No. 26 of 1977 was vacated and as such the decree in the said suit became infructuous but set aside the decree of the trial Court on an erroneous view that the petitioner had no locus standi and cause of action for filing the suit as no relief was sought against him in Title Suit No. 26 of 1977. 

 3. It appears from the copy of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 26 of 1977 that defendant-opposite party Nos. 2-5 were restrained by an order of perpetual injunction from interfering with the work of the opposite party No. 1 as Nikah Registrar and giving effect to the order dated 10.1.77 cancelling his temporary licence. 

 4. It is true that a Nikah Registrar is appointed under Rule 5(1) of the said Rules "on purely temporary basis until a Nikah Registrar is licensed by the Government on regular basis." So the said decree passed in Title Suit No. 26 of 1977 is contrary to the said Rule. Hence observation of the Court of appeal below that with the appointment of plaintiff-petitioner as permanent Nikah Registrar decree passed in Title Suit No. 26 of 1977 has become infructuous is correct interpretation of law. But so long a decree remains un-challenged even if it is illegal that may create complications and is binding upon the parties. It has already been noticed that the plaintiff-petitioner was compelled to file the suit as he was directed by the Deputy Commissioner, Bhola to take steps against the decree passed in Title Suit No. 26 of 1977. Undoubtedly, the said decree has been adversely affecting the petitioner and interfering with his functioning as a Nikah Registrar. In that view of the matter, Court of appeal below was not justified to set aside judgment and decree of the trial Court on the view that the petitioner was not a necessary party in the earlier suit and no relief was sought against him. When a decree adversely affects a person not a party to the same he may file a suit for declaring the same not binding on him and get the same set aside if found illegal as in the present case. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree are set aside and those of the trial Court restored.
